title: O05 — OTP delivery — one fenced SMS login arm, email absent from the marketing site
why: Two rows about how a verification code reaches a person, and both are narrower than their names suggest. `S-733` is a single `case 'send_sms': case 'verify_sms':` arm of the Beget edge relay that returns `{"success":false,"error":"sms_disabled"}` (api-proxy.sanitized.php L181-185) — a server-side fail-closed refusal of the retired *login-time* action names, not an SMS ban. The same file, further down, carries the live SMS OTP send (`S-734` `auth_phone_start`, «SMS через YClients», L307-328); its consumption counterpart (`S-735` `cabinet_link_phone`) sits in the same package K12 but in a different file, the client-consent proxy. `S-740` is a proven absence — `сайт и приложение/index.html` has **0** occurrences of `email` at all, no input, no `mailto:`, no route — but it is an absence in the marketing site only: `app.html` ships a complete two-step email→code login sheet with a multi-tenant business picker (`S-004`, canonical owner «auth / email OTP / business picker»), which K15 decides, not this group. Neither row names a capability today, which is the only reason either is in front of you for signature; what is signed is the owner column, and that column has to be scoped to what each row actually is. The fence also carries conflict C2 on its face — its comment tells the reader that login is «только ВКонтакте / Telegram», while the VK ID login routes in the next lines of the same file are live and routable (`S-737`) against CLAUDE.md rule 7. That conflict is raised here, not resolved, and signing does not settle it.
disappear: Nothing — no code in this group is built, deleted or re-pointed. The fence arm in particular must not be tidied away later: `S-733`'s own rationale records that deleting it would silently re-open an SMS login path, so its parity proof is the negative test that it still refuses.
remain: The fenced arm exactly as it is, refusing server-side in the relay. The live SMS OTP path around it — `S-734` send, `S-735` consumption — stays live and untouched; nothing in this group fences it, and the owner sentence must not be read as closing the SMS channel. The email absence stays an absence **in `index.html`**; the `app.html` email-code sheet (`S-004`) stays live and belongs to K15. STEP_UP_VERIFIED stays unreachable under the frozen limitations, and the reason on record is that the mechanism itself is missing and owned by no package (`MG-P-12`, «NONE — outside the sixteen», alongside the absent verification ladder `MG-P-11`) — not that no code-delivery channel exists. This group must not re-justify that limitation on channel grounds in either direction. On `S-733` the only cell requiring a signature is the owner cell. Its successor, «Connections (class-s destination)», is derived from the row's class rather than chosen — 28 of the 30 class-s rows carry a class-derived destination drawn from the same fixed set of five, and all 30 share one parityRequirement — so it is a pointer, not a decision, and it is not what is being signed. Its «RETIRE FROM PRIMARY NAV — K16» condition binds nothing here, because neither row is in primary nav.
risk: MEDIUM — nothing moves in Wave 1, but the owner column is the durable artifact and the packages that touch this code read it downstream. Scoped as above it is safe; read loosely it is not, and both loose readings are live: «SMS OTP is fenced» maps a channel K12 still runs (`S-734` send, `S-735` consumption) as closed, and «email OTP has no implementation» contradicts the login sheet `app.html` ships today (`S-004`). What holds this above LOW is that the fence's own stated guarantee does not yet exist: `S-733` says its parity proof is the negative test that it still refuses, and no such test is in this checkout — `sms_disabled` appears only in the sanitized relay fixture, which is itself marked «never execute or deploy», and in evidence files. The parity harness offers no comfort either way: `S-733` is RED on all six gates, as all 795 rows are, because the harness emits RED by default and reads evidence rather than checkboxes. Nothing here is irreversible in this wave, which is why it is not higher.
user_impact: For these two rows only, nobody — owner, master or client — notices anything: neither is a screen anybody opens. `send_sms` / `verify_sms` already fail closed server-side in the Beget relay (`{"success":false,"error":"sms_disabled"}`, api-proxy.sanitized.php L181-185, verified), and S-740's absence is real but narrowly scoped — `сайт и приложение/index.html` has zero occurrences of the string `email` at all (0 hits, no input, no `mailto:`, no `email_code` / `magic_link` route). Two corrections to the framing. (1) The group sentence "email OTP / magic-link has no implementation" is false at product level and must be narrowed to index.html: `сайт и приложение/app.html` ships a complete two-step email→code login sheet (S-004, `lgEmailBusinesses` L6331, sheet at L6325/L8383, error strings `email_code_invalid` / `email_code_expired` / `email_code_missing` / `email_too_many_attempts` / `email_login_invalid` at L7619-7623), whose canonical owner is literally "auth / email OTP / business picker". That surface carries a recorded user-visible loss — S-004's parityRiskNote says retiring it strands multi-tenant owners with no business picker — but it is decided in K15, not here. (2) Drop "signing in is the same social-login path it is today": that is a product-level claim O05 does not own and does not establish; sign-in composition is settled by S-004/K15. O05 is pure attribution for two rows: one server-side refusal that stays refusing, and one absence that is an absence *in index.html*.
security_impact: Direction is not inverted — S-733 is already a server-side fail-closed arm in the edge relay, not a client-side check, so nothing migrates from client to server and no hole closes; the arm is kept verbatim. The real subtractive exposure stands and is worth keeping: the arm looks like dead code, and deleting it during a relay rebuild would silently re-open an SMS login path, so its parity proof must be the negative test that it still refuses. But the supporting claim that it "is the sole login-SMS handler" is wrong by construction — the grep was bounded to the literal token `send_sms`. The same file and the same package K12 carry two LIVE SMS OTP rows: S-734 "SMS OTP delivery — auth_phone_start (live, YClients-backed)" (proxy → `/api/auth/phone/start`, L307-328, comment "SMS через YClients") and S-735 "SMS OTP consumption — cabinet_link_phone" (via package5-client-consent-proxy.php). SMS OTP is therefore alive in this system, and O05's owner sentence must not be read as "the SMS channel is fenced" — it fences one arm of three. The correct reading: the fenced pair owns only the retired login-time `send_sms`/`verify_sms` action names; delivery and consumption of SMS codes for phone binding remain live and are owned by S-734/S-735. No frozen limitation is contradicted: fail-closed stays fail-closed, Gate 10 untouched, approval remains role-gated not separation-of-duties, GAP-ATTENDANCE-CONFIRM untouched, and neither row moves STEP_UP_VERIFIED toward reachable — though note that "STEP_UP would need a channel it does not have" is not the reason STEP_UP is unreachable, since S-734/S-735 are exactly such a channel; the frozen limitation stands on its own grounds and should not be re-justified here. Tenant isolation, consent records and audit trails are untouched by both rows.
